who: Historian of modern European intellectual history and France at UNC Chapel Hill; PhD Cornell, 1983.

evidence.says: LC identifies Lloyd S. Kramer as a UNC Chapel Hill history professor specializing in modern European intellectual history; records Lloyd Kramer as a name variant.
Advisory biography identifies UNC history professor Lloyd Kramer and lists his Cornell PhD in 1983.
The 2024 profile says Kramer joined Carolina in 1986 and specializes in modern European history, especially nineteenth-century France.

notes: Authority identity, doctorate institution/year, field and UNC career through the student years agree.

who: Historian of Indigenous North America and the Wendat diaspora at the University of Saskatchewan; PhD Ohio State, 2011.

evidence.says: LC identifies Kathryn Magee Labelle, author of Dispersed but Not Destroyed, as a University of Saskatchewan history faculty member.
The fall 2018 New Researcher Award biography says Labelle received her Ohio State PhD in 2011 and joined Saskatchewan history in 2012.
The repository names Labelle, Kathryn as advisor of Kelly, Mckelvey, Landscapes of Love: Wandat Women and the Politics of Removal, 1795-1910, a Saskatchewan history PhD submitted in August 2024.

notes: The full-name authority, doctorate and direct dissertation-advisor record agree. The repository gives the title end year as 1910, versus 1909 in the supplied records.

who: Historian of Napoleonic warfare at the University of North Texas during the student years; history PhD Florida State, 1997.

evidence.says: LC identifies Michael V. Leggiere as author of Napoleon and the Struggle for Germany and professor of history/deputy director of the Military History Center at UNT in 2015.
UNT lists Michael V. Leggiere in History with a Florida State history PhD, 1997, specializing in the French Revolution and Napoleon.
His institution-hosted CV lists UNT history appointments from 2008 onward, including associate professor in 2011-2015 and professor from 2015.

notes: LC identity, doctorate and UNT employment throughout 2014-2020 agree.

who: Historian of the US-Mexico borderlands at Texas Tech; PhD University of Texas at Austin, 2007.

evidence.says: LC identifies Miguel Antonio Levario, author of Militarizing the Border, as a Texas Tech history assistant professor with a University of Texas PhD.
Texas Tech identifies Miguel A. Levario as a history faculty member specializing in US-Mexico borderlands, with a PhD from UT Austin; the book description uses Miguel Antonio Levario.
The 2015-2016 catalog lists Miguel A. Levario as associate professor of history, appointed in 2007, with a Texas PhD in 2007.

notes: The full-name authority, matching book, doctorate and Texas Tech appointment agree.

who: Judith A. Miller, historian of France at Emory University; PhD Duke, 1987.

evidence.says: LC identifies Judith A. Miller at Emory as author of Mastering the Market: The State and the Grain Trade in Northern France, 1700-1860.

Emory identifies the same author, with a Duke doctorate in French history, and explicitly lists Dana Irwin (2013), Scott Gavorsky (2009), Jayme Feagin (2009) and Dwain Pruitt (2005) as former dissertation students.
The Emory catalog lists Judith Miller, associate professor, with a Duke PhD in 1987.
The alternate candidate J. Hillis Miller is identified in LC as an English scholar with a Harvard PhD in English, 1952.

notes: Direct matches to all four students establish p-115046. Reject p-106312 (J. Hillis Miller), whose name, field and doctorate differ.

who: Historian of eighteenth-century Britain at the University of North Texas; history PhD University of London, 1988.

evidence.says: The candidate ORCID names Marilyn Morris, lists History employment at UNT beginning in 1991, and a History PhD at RHBNC, University of London, completed in 1988.
UNT identifies Marilyn Morris as major professor/chair of Chloe Aubra Northrop's December 2015 history PhD, Fashioning Society in Eighteenth-century British Jamaica.
The Denton Record-Chronicle obituary describes a specialist in eighteenth-century British history, a London history PhD in 1988, and UNT history employment beginning in 1991.
The alternate LC authority identifies M. Michelle Jarrett Morris (Mary Michelle Jarrett Morris), including a 2009 thesis co-advisor role at the University of Missouri-Columbia.

notes: The candidate ORCID and direct dissertation record agree. Reject p-60147: its authority identifies M. Michelle Jarrett Morris, a different scholar.

who: Kathryn Norberg, UCLA historian of early modern France and European women; PhD Yale.

evidence.says: LC identifies Kathryn Norberg, author of Rich and Poor in Grenoble, with a UCLA history appointment and research on European women before 1800 and French court material culture.
UCLA identifies the same historian, lists Rich and Poor in Grenoble and the matching research fields, and records UCLA roles in 1992-1996 and 1998-1999.
UCLA lists Kathryn Norberg with a Yale PhD dated 1979.
The indexed abstract of Christine Ryan Hilliard's 2020 UCLA dissertation, By Choice or By Circumstance: Singlewomen in Early Modern France, names Professor Kathryn Norberg as chair.

notes: Name, authority-linked work, UCLA affiliation and direct student match establish identity. Preserve the degree-year discrepancy: UCLA says 1979, supplied AHA record says 1978.

who: Glen Peterson, historian of modern China at the University of British Columbia; doctorate UBC.

evidence.says: LC identifies Glen Peterson, author of The Power of Words (1997), with the Department of History at the University of British Columbia.
UBC identifies Glen Peterson as a modern China historian and lists The Power of Words: Literacy and Revolution in South China among his books.
The UBC journal biography says Glen Peterson obtained his doctorate at UBC and specializes in modern Chinese history.
In The Great Exodus from China, Dominic Meng-Hsuan Yang thanks his mentors at UBC and explicitly names Glen Peterson as his dissertation supervisor.

notes: LC-linked book, UBC affiliation, doctorate institution and direct student acknowledgement agree. The doctorate year 1991 was not independently confirmed.
